candidate_relations.label: Arachnoid cyst
candidate_relations.reason: The T1 hyperintensity relative to CSF excludes a simple arachnoid cyst. Neurenteric cysts contain proteinaceous or mucoid fluid causing T1 shortening, whereas arachnoid cysts follow CSF signal on all sequences. Both are non-enhancing extra-axial cystic lesions in the posterior fossa, making this a related but conflicting subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Arachnoid cysts are CSF-isointense on all sequences; this lesion is hyperintense to CSF on both T1 and T2, which is incompatible with a simple arachnoid cyst and characteristic of a proteinaceous/mucoid neurenteric cyst

candidate_relations.label: Schwannoma
candidate_relations.reason: The absence of enhancement, cystic MRI signal hyperintense to CSF on T1 and T2, and well-circumscribed cistern location without an identifiable nerve of origin are inconsistent with schwannoma, which typically enhances and arises from a cranial nerve.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Schwannomas are solid or heterogeneously enhancing nerve-sheath tumors; this lesion is cystic, non-enhancing, and hyperintense to CSF on T1

candidate_relations.label: Meningioma
candidate_relations.reason: Meningioma would be expected to enhance intensely, be isointense to gray matter on T2, and have a dural tail. This lesion shows no enhancement and has signal characteristics of a proteinaceous cyst, making meningioma incompatible.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Meningiomas are solid, dural-based, avidly enhancing lesions; this lesion is cystic, non-enhancing, and T1-hyperintense to CSF

candidate_relations.label: Hemangioblastoma
candidate_relations.reason: Hemangioblastoma characteristically shows avid enhancement of a mural nodule, is intra-axial, and is associated with flow voids. The non-enhancing, extra-axial, T1-hyperintense cystic nature of this lesion is entirely inconsistent with hemangioblastoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hemangioblastomas are highly vascular, enhancing tumors typically intra-axial in the cerebellum; this lesion is extra-axial, cystic, non-enhancing, and T1-hyperintense to CSF

case_quality_flags: Classic neurenteric cyst presentation: extra-axial posterior fossa cyst hyperintense to CSF on T1 and T2, non-enhancing, with susceptibility focus, in a young woman with long-standing symptoms
CTA vessel displacement without encasement supports benign extra-axial cystic lesion rather than neoplasm
